$what: Size baselines for the compiled island chunks, measured on the first green chunked build. `node smoke/budgets.mjs --update` rewrites the sizes and the date; `node smoke/budgets.mjs` checks against them, and so does `node smoke/check.mjs`.
$howToRead: `chunk:<name>` is one emitted file. `page:<island>` is what a page carrying only that island downloads: its own chunk plus the shared one, which is the number chunking exists to move. `page:showcase` is the one page carrying more than one island -- life, sand and mines together -- so it is the app's largest JavaScript payload and the only page number not derivable from a single island. A chunk is bigger than the same island's share of one combined module because it carries its own import declarations and compresses on its own; that cost is paid once per island and saved on every island a page does not have.
$tolerance: The band a measured gzip size may exceed its baseline by before the budget fails. The emitter's output moves for reasons that are nobody's regression; what a budget catches is the growth that is.
$whyTheseMoved: Re-measured on 2026-07-31 for two reasons. The first is a correction: until jsc-build learned to follow `#[path]` module declarations, an island edit did not rerun the build script, so the chunks the previous baseline was stamped from were older than the island sources; `chunk:shared` in particular was missing `Range::contains` and its `RangeBounds` machinery, which `island/life.rs` and `island/mines.rs` have both reached since they were written. `smoke/compiled.mjs` now reads the newest OUT_DIR rather than the first by name, so a stale one cannot be measured again. The second is real growth with a cause: `island/sand.rs` iterates its pointer-event array BY VALUE again, which pulls `core::array::IntoIter` into `chunk:sand` and costs it about 470 raw bytes.
